  I essentially follow [this walkthrough](https://nrennie.rbind.io/blog/coloured-text-legend-ggplot-ggtext-marquee) by Nicole Rennie. Note that getting the `element_marquee` to render properly required up to date versions of R and RStudio as of 6/16/2024.





::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(glue)
library(ggplot2)
library(marquee)
theme_set(ggpubr::theme_pubr())

set.seed(1)
```
:::

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
bar_df <- iris |>
  # Let's collect 25 specimens while pretending that the iris dataset is our population
  slice_sample(n = 25) |>
  count(Species) |>
  mutate(
    Species = Species |>
      as.character() |>
      snakecase::to_any_case(case = "sentence"),
    percentage = scales::label_percent()(n/sum(n)),
    my_label = glue("{n} ({percentage})")
  )

my_palette <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(length(bar_df$Species),"Set1")
names(my_palette) <- unique(bar_df$Species)

make_group_string <- function(my_palette){
  # Need to format my groups into a single string that uses marquee
  # syntax to color the appropriate bits
  formatted_strings <- glue(
    "{.[my_palette] [names(my_palette)]}",
    .open = "[",
    .close = "]"
  )

  all_but_last <- formatted_strings[1:(length(formatted_strings) - 1)]
  last_element <- formatted_strings[length(formatted_strings)]

  paste(all_but_last,collapse = ", ") |>
    paste0(", and ",last_element)
}

bar_df |>
  mutate(
    y_label = n + max(n)/20
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Species,y = n,fill = Species,label = my_label)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(y = y_label)) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Species",values = my_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    "# collected",
    breaks = seq(0,10,2),
    limits = c(0,10)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "What is the distribution of iris species in our sample?",
    subtitle = glue::glue("The species collected include {make_group_string(my_palette)}")
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.subtitle = element_marquee(),
    legend.position = "None"
  )
```
